title: Scratch Film — An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Incision
scenes.purpose: Cut a bulb silhouette into opaque dark film stock in successive scratch exposures.
visuals: Opaque blue-black film stock with stationary seeded grain and sprocket holes
First exposure cuts the bulb outline, filament and base rings
Diagonal hatch scratches fill the globe so brightness comes from scratch density
Second and third offset exposures re-cut the outline

beats.development: First thick incision traces the bulb outline; hatch scratches begin inside the globe.
Second and third exposures re-cut the silhouette slightly displaced; hatch density completes the bright globe.

scenes.title: Connection
scenes.purpose: The idea radiates and its scratched lines extend into a connected network.
visuals: Short radiating scratches around the bulb
Teal (#76E1CB) edges cut in sequence from the bulb to six nodes
Each node scratched as a ring and cross on arrival
Sparse teal hatching fills the two network cells

beats.development: Rays flare from the bulb while teal edges cut outward to the first nodes.
Remaining edges and nodes close the system; cells fill with teal scratch density; title fades in on the solid caption band.
captions: AN IDEA BECOMES A CONNECTED SYSTEM

scenes.title: Hold
scenes.purpose: Settled recognisable silhouette and readable title.
visuals: Complete bulb and network held; only small seeded exposure flicker and faint film-wear scratches remain

beats.development: Settled hold of the full composition and title.
captions: AN IDEA BECOMES A CONNECTED SYSTEM

findings: Silhouette carved in three exposures in under 1.2 s, network built in ~1 s, all motion settled by 2.4 s.
justifiedHolds: 2.4–3.0 s hold lets the silhouette and title be recognised and read.

notes: No reviewed preview recipes are listed in STYLE.json (tech.preview_recipes absent, task lists []); the preview demonstrates the core characteristic action: successive incision exposures establishing a silhouette on dark stock.
Scratch emulsion, grain and wear are procedural Canvas 2D approximations of physical scratch film.
